title: "Timer was not added to the SceneTree" misleading in some situations
body:
### Tested versions

v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-3570K CPU @ 3.40GHz (4 Threads)

### Issue description

I ran into an issue where I was getting an odd "Timer was not added to the SceneTree" error message when `start()` is called even though the timer was clearly added to the scene tree and never removed. After a few hours of debugging and looking through the Godot's source code, it turns out that I was getting the message because `start()` was being called while the timer's parent was being deleted (i.e. exiting the scene tree). The specific situation is the following (also in the MRP below):
1. The *buggy* (`Node2D`) scene has two children - an `Area2D` and a `Timer`. `Area2D`'s `body_exited` signal is connected to a function that calls timer's `start()` function. **The order of children matters!** The `Timer` node has to be **after** the `Area2D` node.
2. In the main scene, there's an instance of the *buggy* scene, and another node which is a `CharacterBody2D` that is in the *buggy*'s Area2D.
3. The main scene then calls `queue_free()` on the *buggy* instance.

This will generate the error message from the title. This is because the `Timer` starts exiting the tree first (children are processed in reversed order when leaving the tree) and is marked as "not in the tree" (even though it's still a child of it's parent). After that, when the same happens for the `Area2D` node, it fires a `body_exited` signal for every body that was in it before leaving the tree (not sure if this is desirable), which causes the call to `start()` which results in the error message.

Now, I don't see anything specifically wrong with this setup, but please tell me if I'm missing something. The `Timer` is in the scene tree and the parent was deleted using `queue_free()` which is used to make sure the deletion happens when it's fine to happen. So I strongly feel this really shouldn't happen. It's additionally confusing that whether you'll see the message or not depends on the order of children in the scene that isn't really relevant to the project itself.

I'm not sure what the fix should be, but I have a few ideas that seem sensible to me:
- The `body_exited` signal never gets triggered when the `Area2D` is leaving the tree. This makes sense to me, because I can't think of a scenario where you are deleting the node and still want this signal triggered, but I'm also pretty sure this would break some projects, so I'm not sure how likely this is.
- We get a different error message in the `Timer` for this specific situation. Given that the fix isn't that difficult, this might be fine, but the error message really needs to be better. While debugging, because of the misleading message, I spent some time checking whether the `Timer` was added to the scene (it clearly was), whether I removed it at some point (I clearly didn't), whether it was still the child of it's initial parent at the moment the `start()` is called etc. This is the point I realized that the removal of a node and it's children from a scene is not an "atomic" operation with regards to signals and similar stuff and things can happen during it. So a better message would have definitely helped.
- I think I'd be happy with any other solution that either makes that code work without an error (this would be preferred) or points me to a fix in much more straightforward way.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the MRP (open the project in editor and press `F5`).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[timer-bug-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20148534/timer-bug-project.zip)
